newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CanWest may still breach rules - ABA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CanWest may still breach rules - ABA.

text.p: Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp may still be in breach of broadcasting rules even if it cuts its economic interest in Australia's Ten television network to 57.5 percent from its current 76 percent, the Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Wednesday.

Webb said in its recently concluded investigation into control of the Ten television network, the ABA found Canwest had financed the acquisition of over 37 percent of shares in the Ten Group by a number of companies.
It also found that Canwest was in a position to exercise control over the votes cast by these companies at a Ten meeting.
"As a result, the ABA found that Canwest had company interests of 52.5 percent in the Ten Group Ltd and was in a position to exercise control of the Ten network television licences," Webb said.

"In order to remedy the breaches of the Act identified by the ABA, Canwest must take action so that it no longer has company interests in Ten Group Ltd in excess of 15 percent and is no longer in a position to control Ten Group Ltd," he said.
Webb said the ABA would assess any action taken by Canwest in light of all the facts and circumstances which exist at the relevant time.
"These will include the composiiton of the board of Ten Group Ltd and the identity and structure of any new shareholders in Ten Group Ltd," he said.
The ABA had given Canwest until October 3 this year to rectify the breaches.
Canwest said earlier this month it disagreed with the Australian government's ruling regarding its stake in the Ten Group and would seek clarification.
